question: Why does the rule "Follow one team-wide formatting style, enforced by a formatter" matter in a code review?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Follow one team-wide formatting style, enforced by a formatter
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 6: Formatting, PR review rules
Follow one team-wide formatting style, enforced by a formatter

relevant_concepts: Follow one team-wide formatting style, enforced by a formatter

Formatting is communication. A reader needs to trust that a formatting gesture in one file means the same thing in another, and inconsistent style makes the code look as if disagreeing individuals wrote it. The team should agree on a single set of rules once, encode them in the formatter, and follow them even when they aren't your preference. The code itself is the best coding standard document.

Separate distinct concepts with blank lines

relevant_concepts: Separate distinct concepts with blank lines
Code is read top to bottom, and each group of lines is a complete thought. A blank line is a visual cue for a new, separate concept, and removing the blank lines has a remarkably obscuring effect.

question: Why does the rule "Keep closely related lines together" matter in a code review?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Keep closely related lines together
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 6: Formatting, PR review rules
Keep closely related lines together

relevant_concepts: If openness separates concepts, density implies association. Tightly related lines should look dense so the reader can take them in at a glance. Distracting comments between related fields break their association and force extra eye and head movement.
